title: Open Order Value as a Profile-Level Exposure Figure
content:
Open order value on Northbeam Purchase Orders and Fulfilment is the total of the order totals of that profile's orders
standing placed, awaiting stock, scheduled or out for delivery. It is read at the moment of handling, across the whole
profile, with no historical window and no order-by-order reading.

## What the figure governs

Open order value governs how much may be taken on deposit and whether a further large order is accepted without
payment cleared. The basis on which money is taken, the deposit taken on placement and the ways the order may be paid
for are those of the fulfilment service the order was placed under.

Where the profile pays on a financing account, the open value is set against the room left on that account, and an
order beyond that room is held until the customer pays another way. A business profile on invoice terms has its open
value set against its net terms, and an overdue invoice stops further orders being accepted on invoice.

## What counts and what drops out

Orders awaiting stock count toward open value at their full amount, because the price is held. Cancelled orders and
orders returned to stock drop out of the count on the day they close.

## The figure worked through (hypothetical order totals)

A profile holds three orders in the standings above, with totals of 900.00, 1500.00 and 300.00. Added together these
give an open order value of 2700.00; the middle order, sitting awaiting stock, counts at its full 1500.00 and not at
some reduced figure. On the day the order of 1500.00 is cancelled it drops out, and the profile's open order value
reads 1200.00 from that day.

## Points of judgement

**Is the figure read per order or per profile?** Per profile, across every order of that profile standing placed,
awaiting stock, scheduled or out for delivery.

**Does an order still waiting for a shipment count less?** No, it counts at its full amount, the price being held.

**On what day does a closed order leave the figure?** The day it closes, whether it was cancelled or the goods went
back to stock.
